## Select outgoing acoustic and advected perturbations (`outflow`) {#sec-ch11-outflow}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

Local symbols: $\mathbf W^{\mathrm{bg}}$ denotes the saved initial boundary background, which is distinct
from the well-balanced reference. $v_{\mathrm{out}}$ is outward velocity [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$]; $Z_{\mathrm{ac}}$
is acoustic impedance [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$]; $a_+$ and $a_-$ are acoustic perturbations
[$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$]; $d_{\mathrm{ent}}$ is the advected density combination [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$];
$\alpha_{\mathrm{bc}}$ is a dimensionless admissibility factor. All are proposed in the chapter's notation issue.
A prefix $\delta$ below means subtraction of this background, not the centroid offset $\delta_i$.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Build primitive ghosts from the saved initial background plus outgoing perturbations. A shared factor keeps hydro composition and tracers admissible.
Default: off; external faces default reflecting.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

Freeze an admissible background and an outward Cartesian face frame. Linearized mass, normal momentum and
pressure equations have material derivatives proportional respectively to minus background density, minus
inverse background density and minus background density times squared sound speed, all multiplying the
appropriate normal derivative. For the outer x1 face, write the frozen material derivative as
$\mathrm D/\mathrm Dt=\partial_t+v_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{bg}}\partial_1$.
The three equations are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm D\delta\rho}{\mathrm Dt}&=-\rho^{\mathrm{bg}}\partial_1\delta v_{\mathrm{out}},\\
\frac{\mathrm D\delta v_{\mathrm{out}}}{\mathrm Dt}&=-\frac{1}{\rho^{\mathrm{bg}}}\partial_1\delta p,\\
\frac{\mathrm D\delta p}{\mathrm Dt}&=-\rho^{\mathrm{bg}}(c_s^{\mathrm{bg}})^2\partial_1\delta v_{\mathrm{out}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Eliminating the pressure and velocity coupling gives the combinations

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_{\mathrm{ac}}&=\rho^{\mathrm{bg}}c_s^{\mathrm{bg}},\\
a_\pm&=\delta v_{\mathrm{out}}\pm\delta p/Z_{\mathrm{ac}},\\
d_{\mathrm{ent}}&=\delta\rho-\delta p/(c_s^{\mathrm{bg}})^2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-outflow-modes}

Adding/subtracting the linearized momentum equation and the pressure equation divided by impedance yields
transport of $a_\pm$ at the two acoustic speeds; subtracting the pressure equation divided by squared sound
speed from continuity cancels its divergence term and leaves advection of $d_{\mathrm{ent}}$.
Integrating each constant-coefficient transport equation over a boundary-adjacent cell gives its incoming
minus outgoing face transport. A characteristic entering from outside has no interior-determined perturbation:
the boundary chooses zero perturbation for that incoming mode. The code uses the *current* outward velocity
and sound speed for this selector, while @eq-ch11-outflow-modes uses the background impedance and sound speed.
Thus it is a locally linear characteristic prescription, not the exact nonlinear exterior solution.

Keep $a_+$ when $v_{\mathrm{out}}+c_s\ge0$, keep $a_-$ when $v_{\mathrm{out}}-c_s\ge0$, and otherwise set each
to zero. Keep $d_{\mathrm{ent}}$, tangential velocity, composition and tracer-ratio perturbations when
$v_{\mathrm{out}}\ge0$; otherwise set them to zero. Equality selects the outgoing branch. Invert the split:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta v_{\mathrm{out}}&=(a_++a_-)/2,\\
\delta p&=Z_{\mathrm{ac}}(a_+-a_-)/2,\\
\delta\rho&=d_{\mathrm{ent}}+\delta p/(c_s^{\mathrm{bg}})^2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-outflow-inverse}

`plus`, `minus` and `entropy` ([`bc_func.cpp:135-165`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L135-L165)) implement both @eq-ch11-outflow-modes and @eq-ch11-outflow-inverse.
For the lower face, reversing the coordinate normal before splitting and reversing it back after inversion
accounts for the sign in the velocity update. The same selected interior perturbation is supplied to every
ghost, but each ghost retains its own saved background.

For any lower-bounded component $q$ with floor $q_{\min}$, admissibility requires
$q^{\mathrm{bg}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{bc}}\delta q\ge q_{\min}$.
If $\delta q<0$, division gives the bound $(q^{\mathrm{bg}}-q_{\min})/(-\delta q)$;
otherwise that component imposes no reduction. Start with one, take the minimum of all bounds, multiply each
binding bound below one by 0.99, and clamp the result to $[0,1]$. Apply this to density, pressure, every $y_n$,
the complement $1-\sum_n y_n$, and every passive tracer ratio $r_n$. Nonnegative complement enforces the
composition sum. The same factor multiplies every perturbation, including tracers:

$$
\mathbf W^{\mathrm{ghost}}=\mathbf W^{\mathrm{bg,ghost}}+
\alpha_{\mathrm{bc}}\delta\mathbf W.
$$ {#eq-ch11-outflow-admissible}

`alpha` ([`bc_func.cpp:167-207`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L167-L207)) implements @eq-ch11-outflow-admissible. Convexity of these linear inequalities proves
admissibility for an admissible background in exact arithmetic. It proves neither a positive temperature
for every EOS nor nonlinear nonreflection. C2 checks the invertible acoustic algebra; C3 verifies the shared
limiter against independent inequality bounds, including a species-complement and tracer-limited case.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

Capture the background before the first physical fill, including initialized ghost values. Transform
both current and saved velocities to the face frame, compute a perturbation from the nearest owned cell,
select outgoing modes, limit each ghost, then transform back. The operator writes only ghosts.
Conserved calls go through `apply_boundaries`: consecutive outflow faces share a primitive conversion;
before another callback, pending faces are converted and flushed. Tracer densities use dry density, not
primitive total density. The cartoon shows mode directions and the convex contraction separately.
No coupled wall/seam convergence or reflection measurement is reported here.

@fig-ch11-outflow-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch11-outflow-stencil
#| fig-cap: "Select outgoing acoustic and advected perturbations. Schematic only; no simulation measurements."
#| fig-alt: "Labelled schematic of the outflow boundary operation; ghosts and owned cells have separate text labels."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch11.fig_outflow_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Implementation sites for outflow. {#tbl-ch11-outflow-code}

1. Use the scalar/shallow-water fallback first. Otherwise require EOS, coordinates and a saved same-shape reference. The anchor `radiating` is in [`bc_func.cpp:108-133`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L108-L133).
2. Require a supported EOS, primitive type, finite input, positive finite sound speeds, and admissible background density, pressure and composition. The anchor `check_background` is in [`bc_func.cpp:92-106`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L92-L106).
3. Split in the face frame, select modes using current speeds, and reconstruct the selected perturbation. The anchor `plus` is in [`bc_func.cpp:135-165`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L135-L165).
4. Validate tracer background shape, finiteness and nonnegativity; reduce the shared factor and verify reconstructed ghosts are finite. The anchor `alpha` is in [`bc_func.cpp:167-207`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L167-L207).
5. Flush conserved pending faces in face order using dry-density tracer conversion. The anchor `apply_boundaries` is in [`meshblock.cpp:1441-1519`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1441-L1519).

### Limits

Outflow is skipped by the tangential corner refresh ([`meshblock.cpp:951-978`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L951-L978)). The gravity-work fixer is not an open-boundary
energy budget: its x1 mass-crossing check can reject an open boundary; the error directs users to
`gravity-work-fixer: false` ([`meshblock.cpp:850-907`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L850-L907)). The implicit closure remains reflecting in the cited operator, so a
characteristic ghost fill does not establish a characteristic implicit boundary. The test's restart continuation
and missing-reference rejection are explicit in `restart_continuation_and_missing_reference` ([`test_radiating_boundary.cpp:445-468`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_radiating_boundary.cpp#L445-L468)).
Saved backgrounds are fixed initialization data; adaptive exterior evolution is not implemented by this callback.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
